variable_meanings.Z: Binary randomized encouragement to use a process setting.
variable_meanings.D: Binary setting actually used, possibly different from encouragement.

data.structural_assumptions: The encouragement Z is jointly independent of all potential settings D(0),D(1) and potential outcomes Y(0),Y(1). Observed setting is D(Z), and observed outcome is Y(D(Z)); encouragement has no direct outcome effect. Every unit has binary potential settings and outcomes, with no interference. Uptake is monotone: D(1)>=D(0). Outcome monotonicity Y(1)>=Y(0) is NOT assumed. Use an unrestricted common population distribution over potential types satisfying those assumptions. The two conditional observation panels constrain the same population law; they are not separate latent populations.
data.data_scope: Project-authored exact conditional population probabilities for a controlled process model, not finite batch counts, experimental observations or estimated probabilities. Sampling uncertainty is outside scope. The table supplies P(D=d,Y=y|Z=z), not joint probabilities requiring an encouragement allocation fraction.
data.research_targets: Report the first-stage uptake difference E[D|Z=1]-E[D|Z=0], intention-to-encourage pass difference E[Y|Z=1]-E[Y|Z=0], and the setting effect among units whose setting follows encouragement, E[Y(1)-Y(0)|D(1)>D(0)]. Also obtain sharp attainable bounds on the whole-population setting effect E[Y(1)-Y(0)] and decide whether that overall effect is necessarily strictly positive. Distinguish a local effect for uptake-switching units from a whole-population effect; do not add an equal-effects or linear constant-effect restriction.
data.reporting: All effects are differences of probability fractions. The sharp interval is [minimum,maximum]. Numeric tolerance1e-8 absolute plus1e-7 relative; Boolean exact. Bounds must be attainable under one common joint potential-type distribution.

provenance.kind: Project-authored controlled nonclinical process example. No observations or numeric results from the cited paper were imported.
provenance.method_read_scope: Author-hosted Balke and Pearl(1997),JASA92:1171-1176,pages1172-1173: latent binary response types, linear constraints/optimization and monotone-uptake restriction. The project model adds the explicitly stated assumptions and derives its own exact bounds; no unrestricted-IV formula is substituted for the monotone model.
